facts.fact: Agence Ecofin reports ARCT's communique of 3 June 2026 requiring Burundian mobile subscribers to regularise SIM identification by 25 June 2026 or have lines deactivated, with only the carte nationale d'identite accepted for the operation, under a ministerial ordinance of 13 January 2026.

facts.fact: Connecting Africa reports mandatory SIM and eSIM registration in Burundi began in mid-June 2026, requiring registrants to present legible, up-to-date identification documents at a registration point, with ARCT interconnecting operators and state bodies for real-time monitoring of registration and user identity.
Connecting Africa reports ARCT's director general said 70% of SIM cards had been registered, over three months after the campaign began; no figure for checks against the national ID is given.

facts.fact: UNCDF's assessment says citizens open bank and mobile money accounts by presenting national IDs, but Burundi has no national identity database to support financial institutions in KYC checks, so account-opening KYC is not checked against an ID register.
